Imagine teaching a young cousin to tell mangoes from bananas. Instead of long rules about shape and color, you just show them many fruits, saying "mango" or "banana" each time. Soon, they learn to identify new fruits on their own! This is just like machine learning.

Computers can't see mangoes directly. They only understand numbers! So, our first big step in machine learning is to turn everything, like a house or a photo, into lists of numbers. These lists are called vectors. Once we have numbers, mathematics can help the computer find hidden rules to learn from.

Let's find the length of a vector like (3, 4). Imagine three steps right, then four steps up. The straight line distance from start to end is the length. Using Pythagoras' theorem, square three and four, add them, then take the square root. That gives us five. Easy!

For your exams, remember the key words like 'loss functions' and 'classification.' Pay attention to details like 'norm' meaning length, not squared length. And know that 'squared loss' is for numbers, while 'zero-one loss' is for categories. Keep practicing turning the world into numbers. You've got this!
